newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down, INRO watches intently.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down, INRO watches intently.

text.p: Malaysia's rubber market ended lower on Tuesday but the five-day average price was still lower than the intervention level set by the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO), traders said.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted August buyers of the benchmark RSS1 at 233.50 Malaysian/Singapore cents (93 U.S. cents) a kg, down 3.50 cents from Monday's close. August SMR20 was half cent down to 235.
The INRO's five-day moving indicator was at 187.60 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on July 7, compared to the 189.97 on July 4.
The daily indicator was at 182.89, against 184.61 previously.
Under INRO's intervention guidelines, 183 cents is the level which the group would consider buying rubber in the market.
"We follow the five-day indicator for interventions and it hasn't reached there yet," a spokeswoman for the rubber body said.
A check with trading houses in the evening showed the SMR20 at offered 230, SMR10 at 232, SMR5 at 243, SMR CV at 302, SMR L at 283 and drum latex at 200.
